fatal_errors: The proposed NaCl pin-on-disk experiment does not reconstruct the deionized-water, temperature-dependent reciprocating comparison between AlCoCrFeNi2.1 and thermally shocked DS2205.

It predicts total loss greater than the sum of wear-only and corrosion-only losses without evidence or a valid component-decomposition protocol; this synergy was not the principal demonstrated result.
The film-enhancing pretreatment may also alter hardness, phase structure, roughness, and residual stress, so it does not cleanly isolate passive-film stability.
explanation: The hypothesis captures one genuine part of the target mechanism: sliding-induced passive-film removal competing with repassivation can couple corrosion and wear. Its boundary statement also appropriately recognizes that rapid film regeneration could defeat the prediction. However, it reduces the governing behavior to a generic positive-feedback model and misses the central nonmonotonic temperature dependence: slow repair and abrasion at 25 °C, optimal film or tribolayer stability and polishing near 50 °C, and repeated oxide-layer fracture plus third-body effects at 100 °C. It also omits the thermally shocked HEA-versus-DS2205 comparison, retention versus redistribution of dual-phase structures, specified loads and frequencies, and the observed order-of-magnitude wear advantage of the HEA. The proposed static-corrosion and inert-wear baselines can estimate tribocorrosion synergy but are not matched to the study's primary comparator. The falsification experiment is directionally useful, yet pretreatment confounding prevents a decisive causal test unless mechanical and microstructural properties are independently matched. No prior evidence is cited, so the claims about superadditive loss and localized corrosion are unsupported in this context.
